segments.text: Turn these two phase controls. The light at the pupil stays equally bright, but the focal pattern moves and spreads.
segments.say: Turn these two phase controls. The light at the pupil stays equally bright, but the focal pattern moves and spreads.

segments.text: The aperture and total power have not changed.
segments.say: The aperture and total power have not changed.

segments.text: Which control should we change to make this pattern match the target?
segments.say: Which control should we change to make this pattern match the target?

segments.text: Predict the image forwards, then carry its error backwards to the design.
segments.say: Predict the image forwards, then carry its error backwards to the design.

segments.text: Here is our one-dimensional pupil, the illuminated opening. We change only its phase, keeping the amplitude fixed.
segments.say: Here is our one-dimensional pupil, the illuminated opening. We change only its phase, keeping the amplitude fixed.

segments.text: The phase contains a linear term for tilt and a quadratic term for defocus. Both coefficients are measured in radians.
segments.say: The phase contains a linear term for tilt and a quadratic term for defocus. Both coefficients are measured in radians.

segments.text: Watch a phase ramp move the focal pattern sideways.
segments.say: Watch a phase ramp move the focal pattern sideways.

segments.text: Add quadratic phase at the same detector plane, and the pattern broadens. Interference redistributes the light.
segments.say: Add quadratic phase at the same detector plane, and the pattern broadens. Interference redistributes the light.

segments.text: Multiply the fixed amplitude by a complex phase factor, rotating the field without changing its magnitude. A unitary Fourier transform propagates it while preserving total sampled power.
segments.say: Multiply the fixed amplitude by a complex phase factor, rotating the field without changing its magnitude. A unitary Fourier transform propagates it while preserving total sampled power.

segments.text: The detector reads squared field magnitude. Across the full detector grid, these normalized intensities add to one.
segments.say: The detector reads squared field magnitude. Across the full detector grid, these normalized intensities add to one.

segments.text: Choose the focused pattern with zero tilt and defocus as our target. Start with tilt and defocus coefficients of one point five and two.
segments.say: Choose the focused pattern with zero tilt and defocus as our target. Start with tilt and defocus coefficients of one point five and two.

segments.text: Subtract the target intensity at every detector sample. These differences are the residuals, including the pattern's faint outer structure.
segments.say: Subtract the target intensity at every detector sample. These differences are the residuals, including the pattern's faint outer structure.

segments.text: Square and sum the residuals, then divide by twice the target's squared norm. This dimensionless loss measures the mismatch.
segments.say: Square and sum the residuals, then divide by twice the target's squared norm. This dimensionless loss measures the mismatch.

segments.text: Keep that target and normalization fixed. Zero loss means matching this sampled intensity, not necessarily recovering a unique phase.
segments.say: Keep that target and normalization fixed. Zero loss means matching this sampled intensity, not necessarily recovering a unique phase.

segments.text: Now ask how a tiny parameter change affects the loss. Follow the same calculation backwards using the chain rule.
segments.say: Now ask how a tiny parameter change affects the loss. Follow the same calculation backwards using the chain rule.

segments.text: A positive residual marks a sample that is too bright. A negative residual marks one that is too dim.
segments.say: A positive residual marks a sample that is too bright. A negative residual marks one that is too dim.

segments.text: Divide each residual by the target's squared norm, and multiply by the focal field. This starts the reverse intensity calculation.
segments.say: Divide each residual by the target's squared norm, and multiply by the focal field. This starts the reverse intensity calculation.

segments.text: Apply the conjugate transpose of the Fourier transform. This gathers every detector sample's influence back at the pupil.
segments.say: Apply the conjugate transpose of the Fourier transform. This gathers every detector sample's influence back at the pupil.

segments.text: This backward field represents mathematical sensitivity. No physical light travels backwards in this calculation.
segments.say: This backward field represents mathematical sensitivity. No physical light travels backwards in this calculation.

segments.text: At the pupil, a small phase change rotates the complex field. That converts field sensitivity into real phase sensitivity.
segments.say: At the pupil, a small phase change rotates the complex field. That converts field sensitivity into real phase sensitivity.

segments.text: Weight this sensitivity by position for tilt, and squared position for defocus. Sum across the pupil to obtain both derivatives, the components of our design gradient.
segments.say: Weight this sensitivity by position for tilt, and squared position for defocus. Sum across the pupil to obtain both derivatives, the components of our design gradient.

segments.text: Check those derivatives before using them. Nudge one coefficient forwards and backwards by the same small amount.
segments.say: Check those derivatives before using them. Nudge one coefficient forwards and backwards by the same small amount.

segments.text: Recompute both losses and divide their difference by the separation. This central finite difference estimates the same local slope.
segments.say: Recompute both losses and divide their difference by the separation. This central finite difference estimates the same local slope.

segments.text: Try several perturbation sizes. Large nudges miss the local slope; extremely small ones expose floating-point rounding.
segments.say: Try several perturbation sizes. Large nudges miss the local slope; extremely small ones expose floating-point rounding.

segments.text: Here both parameter derivatives agree over a useful range. They are evaluated at the identical starting design.
segments.say: Here both parameter derivatives agree over a useful range. They are evaluated at the identical starting design.

segments.text: That checks the implemented derivative. It does not establish that the optical model captures a real device.
segments.say: That checks the implemented derivative. It does not establish that the optical model captures a real device.

segments.text: Move opposite the gradient to seek a lower loss. The step length controls how far we move.
segments.say: Move opposite the gradient to seek a lower loss. The step length controls how far we move.

segments.text: Surprisingly, the first step increases defocus while reducing the loss. The coefficients act together; shrinking each one is not the rule.
segments.say: Surprisingly, the first step increases defocus while reducing the loss. The coefficients act together; shrinking each one is not the rule.

segments.text: Recompute the loss after each trial. Shorten an unsuccessful step, and accept it only when the loss decreases.
segments.say: Recompute the loss after each trial. Shorten an unsuccessful step, and accept it only when the loss decreases.

segments.text: Watch forty updates bring this pattern close to the target, with the same aperture and power throughout.
segments.say: Watch forty updates bring this pattern close to the target, with the same aperture and power throughout.

segments.text: Start both coefficients at three instead. The loss stalls above zero, although we know a zero-loss design exists.
segments.say: Start both coefficients at three instead. The loss stalls above zero, although we know a zero-loss design exists.

segments.text: A correct gradient gives local information, not a guarantee of the best design.
segments.say: A correct gradient gives local information, not a guarantee of the best design.

segments.text: Differentiable optics means an optical model has usable derivatives with respect to its chosen design variables.
segments.say: Differentiable optics means an optical model has usable derivatives with respect to its chosen design variables.

segments.text: Automatic differentiation applies derivative rules through a computation graph. Here, we wrote the reverse calculation explicitly.
segments.say: Automatic differentiation applies derivative rules through a computation graph. Here, we wrote the reverse calculation explicitly.

segments.text: Adjoint methods efficiently carry a scalar objective's sensitivity backwards. An automatic-differentiation system can include an optical solver's adjoint.
segments.say: Adjoint methods efficiently carry a scalar objective's sensitivity backwards. An automatic differentiation system can include an optical solver's adjoint.

segments.text: For curved lenses, the chain must include ray intersections and Snell refraction. Away from grazing incidence, local derivatives follow one intersection branch.
segments.say: For curved lenses, the chain must include ray intersections and Snell refraction. Away from grazing incidence, local derivatives follow one intersection branch.

segments.text: Clipping or switching ray paths can break a smooth local derivative.
segments.say: Clipping or switching ray paths can break a smooth local derivative.

segments.text: For joint optical and digital design, place the loss after reconstruction. Differentiate through both stages to update both sets of parameters.
segments.say: For joint optical and digital design, place the loss after reconstruction. Differentiate through both stages to update both sets of parameters.

segments.text: These are extensions of the chain. Our computed example optimizes only a phase element's intensity pattern.
segments.say: These are extensions of the chain. Our computed example optimizes only a phase element's intensity pattern.

segments.text: Predict fields and measurements forwards. Carry a precisely defined loss backwards to the parameters you can change.
segments.say: Predict fields and measurements forwards. Carry a precisely defined loss backwards to the parameters you can change.

segments.text: Check the derivative, take a step, and measure the loss again.
segments.say: Check the derivative, take a step, and measure the loss again.

segments.text: This model uses one wavelength and ignores polarization. Test what it omits: sensor noise, fabrication limits, and performance beyond the optimized samples.
segments.say: This model uses one wavelength and ignores polarization. Test what it omits: sensor noise, fabrication limits, and performance beyond the optimized samples.

segments.text: Differentiable optics connects image error to design changes. A useful gradient still needs a useful model.
segments.say: Differentiable optics connects image error to design changes. A useful gradient still needs a useful model.
